Profile.label: Profile
Profile.body1: Over the past three years I’ve worked across frontend architecture, backend APIs, databases, mobile applications, authentication, admin dashboards and deployment.
Profile.body2: That range is the point. I can take a business requirement and carry it the whole way — deciding how the data is modelled, what the API has to expose, what the interface needs to do, and how the result gets deployed and kept running. Most of what I’ve shipped runs in production for real businesses.

oson-uy.subtitle: Real Estate Technology Platform
oson-uy.description: A digital platform designed to connect buyers with new residential developments across Uzbekistan.
oson-uy.problem: Buying into a new residential development means working across a dozen developer websites, Instagram pages and phone calls. Prices, floor plans, completion dates and developer credentials all live in different places and different formats, so nothing is genuinely comparable. Buyers needed a simpler way to discover, compare and understand what is actually being built.
oson-uy.solution: Oson Uy brings residential projects, apartments, pricing, floor plans and developer information into one platform. A web application for buyers, a mobile application, and an admin dashboard the catalogue is maintained from — all three reading from the same PostgreSQL database, so what a developer updates is what a buyer sees.
oson-uy.architectureIntro: Three clients, one core. The web app, the mobile app and the admin dashboard all speak to the same NestJS API, which owns the data through Prisma.

Process.label: How I work
Process.body: I enjoy working across the full product lifecycle — from understanding a business problem to designing the architecture, implementing the product and deploying it. The steps below are not a methodology I read about; they are the order things actually happen in when a product has to ship.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: What is the business problem, and who has it?

steps.title: Design
steps.body: What does the product need to do, and what does it not need to do?

steps.title: Architect
steps.body: Data model, API surface, and how the clients share one core.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Frontend, backend and mobile against that shared contract.

steps.title: Test
steps.body: Real data, real devices, real edge cases before anyone else sees it.

steps.title: Deploy
steps.body: Get it into production, with the environment and pipeline set up properly.

steps.title: Improve
steps.body: Watch how it is used and keep changing it. Shipping is the start.
